subject: Hyperserve Gen API: KV cache thrash causing p95 spikes - action map
messages:

Cc: ops@hyperserve.com

Subject: Gen API p95 spike starting 09:05 PST

Chloe,

We started seeing p95 latency for our Gen API requests jump from ~320ms to 1.8s at 09:05 PST. Error rates are low but timeouts have increased across multiple endpoints (create, chat). Attached are traces from 09:05-09:15 and a short sample request id list.

Can you confirm whether any rollout or config change aligns with this window? Our business-critical flows are impacted and we may need an ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Sara Thompson
Head of Engineering, Hyperserve
sara@hyperserve.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Gen API p95 spike starting 09:05 PST

Team,

FYI - Hyperserve reported a p95 spike at 09:05 PST. Sara attached traces. I need SRE + runtime triage asap. Please ack and post initial findings here.

Immediate asks:
- Triage root cause (KV cache vs autoscaler churn vs new model variant)
- If KV thrash, propose short-term mitigations we can toggle without deploy (ttl, cache pin, warmup)
- Customer comms draft for Sara explaining next steps and ETA (30/60/120m)

I'll coordinate the MAP and draft the SLA exception if needed. Meeting in 10 if handy, otherwise reply inline.

Chloe Martin
Sr. Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-06T09:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Gen API p95 spike starting 09:05 PST

Quick notes from initial triage:
- Observed sharp increase in KV cache miss rate starting 09:04:58 for customer Hyperserve (tenant id HS-4492).
- Correlated with a model variant rollout to gen-v2-q that changes KV key namespace; many warm caches were invalidated leading to higher compute per request and autoscaler scaling down/up rapidly (churn) because burst pattern confused cooldown.
- No code deploys at 09:05 in serving plane; rollout was a config-based variant switch that updated model selector table.

Immediate mitigations I can apply (non-deploy):
1) Temporarily pin Hyperserve to gen-v1 until we stabilize (config flip, immediate)
2) Increase KV retention TTL on affected hosts to avoid eviction for 15m (runtime flag)
3) Disable aggressive scale-down (set min replicas for the customer pool to current level)

I'll prepare a diag bundle and will attach it here (diag_bundle_1106.zip).
Estimated time to meaningful impact: pinning variant + increasing TTL should reduce p95 within 10-20m.

Karthik
Senior SRE

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-06T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Gen API p95 spike starting 09:05 PST

Agree with Karthik. Proposed orchestration plan:
- T+0m: Pin Hyperserve to gen-v1 (chloe to approve; change via routing config)
- T+5m: Increase KV TTL on US-W hosts serving HS to 30m
- T+10m: Set min replicas for HS pool = current to avoid scale-down churn
- T+15m: Monitor p50/p95 and QPS; if stable, schedule a canary for gen-v2-q with adjusted cache keys and warmup scripts

Operational notes:
- I'll prepare a temporary routing override and a rate-cap if Hyperserve wants a safety throttle; this is customer-facing and requires chloe to sign off on MAP messaging.
- If we need to escalate to a full SLA exception, chloe should attach the draft to customer comms.

Ben Carter
Runtime Ops

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@hyperserve.com>
Cc: ops@hyperserve.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-06T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Gen API p95 spike starting 09:05 PST - Immediate mitigations and MAP

Sara,

Thanks for flagging this and for the traces. Summary and immediate actions we are taking now:
- Root cause (preliminary): KV cache namespace change after a model variant selector update created cache misses and autoscaler churn. No code deploys to serving plane.
- Immediate mitigations (in flight): pinning your traffic to gen-v1, increasing KV retention TTL on US-West, and preventing scale-down for your pool. Karthik and Ben are applying these now.
- Estimated impact: we expect p95 to drop toward baseline within 10-25 minutes. We'll confirm once metrics show steady improvement.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
1) T+0 - Actions above (in flight). Target: 10:20 PST validate p95.
2) T+60 - If stable, we will perform a controlled canary of gen-v2-q with adjusted cache key handling and warmup; target window 11:00-11:30 PST.
3) T+360 - Post-canary rollback window and follow-up runbook review. We will also provide a draft SLA exception for this incident.

Attachments: sla_exception_draft_Hyperserve.docx (draft for your review), diag_bundle_1106.zip
Please reply ACK to this MAP or let us know a different preference for the canary window.

Apologies for the disruption. We'll keep you posted every 30 minutes or on material changes.

Chloe Martin
Sr. Product Ops
Redwood Inference
